comment: Maps a displaceR binary version label to a published release asset.
The authoritative identity of a build is upstream_sha, not the DISPLACE
version string: include/version.h hardcodes VERSION and is not derived from
git tags, so many different upstream commits all report '1.6.6'.
Entries are added by hand from the step summary of the 'Build DISPLACE
binary' workflow. Bump 'default' only once a build has been smoke-tested;
users who pinned an older version keep working.
'builds' maps a glibc target to an asset. install_displace() picks the
newest build whose glibc requirement is <= the host's glibc.
'versions' is empty until the first release asset is published. Until then
install_displace() will tell the user to point DISPLACE_BINARY at a local
build, or to run the build workflow. See docs/roadmap.md.

note: Upstream tag v1.8.0; the manifest default since 2026-09-23. Model behaviour
differs from 1.6.6 (N depletion, cpue multiplier, area closures, TAC
logic), so results are not comparable across the two. Built with the
ices-optional patch: a missing coord<N>_with_icesrectanglecode.dat no longer
aborts the load. Both payloads bundle their third-party libraries.
Upstream 1.6.6 was never tagged or released: 7f2656fb is v1.6.5
(45f44168) plus 8cda73cc ('v1.6.6 - Fix double counting in nodes
cumcatches', which bumps version.h) and an HPC compile fix.
Same upstream commit as 1.6.6-7f2656fb. The difference is the payload:
this build bundles Boost, GeographicLib and sqlite3 alongside the
binary. 1.6.6-7f2656fb assumed those were present on the host and fails
at startup on a server without the -dev packages installed.
The macOS build is carried over unchanged -- bundling is Linux-only.
